clue.text: Tar pits eventually found on each island

indicators.note: eventually points to what comes at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of pits
EA is the standard abbreviation for each
the Isle of Man, the island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Tar pits turn up on every island in some survey of geology.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar is not the black stuff here but an old word for a sailor, so SEAMAN is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is an old informal word for a sailor, from the tarpaulin hats and tarred clothing sailors wore.

clue.text: Leave hastily when Cliff starts to play Elvis records

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff face

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Fans run for it when Cliff Richard begins playing Elvis songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard and Elvis are both singers, so Cliff looks like a name; here it is a crag. Scarper is British slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is informal British for running off quickly, which is leaving hastily.

clue.text: Woman getting upset over son's crime

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down answer that flips the word so it reads upwards
over here means covering on all sides, so the name wraps around the other letter

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother is distressed about the offence her son committed.
explanation.walkthrough: NORA turned upwards becomes ARON, which then goes around S.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Not entirely kind having article holding up Capone as a loser

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the word loses its final letter
in a down answer, something holding up another sits beneath it, so the other piece goes on top

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
a sort is a kind or type
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A gangster is described as a failure, with a newspaper piece propping him up.
explanation.walkthrough: An also-ran is originally a racehorse that finished out of the places.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a competitor who finished unplaced, hence an unsuccessful person, a loser.

clue.text: Grumble when drinks are sent back

indicators.note: things sent back travel the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: two tots of the spirit made from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Someone complains when their drinks are returned to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A murmur is a low complaint, as in doing something without a murmur, so it is a grumble.

clue.text: Ragamuffin's discovered in church insensible

indicators.note: discovered means found inside, so the letters lie within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A scruffy child has been found unconscious in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a ragged, dirty child, much the same as a street urchin.

clue.text: Star mole abandoned by spymaster causing a state of confusion

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A top double agent is dropped by his handler, throwing the service into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned by' looks like the mole being dropped, but M is added to the letters before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively any turbulent situation of chaos and confusion.

clue.text: One's inclined to cover bad cut

indicators.note: in a down answer, covering another piece means sitting on top of it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a rake is a slope, as of a stage, so one that is inclined
food that has gone bad is off

explanation.surface: Someone feels like hiding a nasty wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a share of profits, often illicit, which is someone's cut of the money.

clue.text: Payment of a fixed allowance by Conservative party

parts.note: Con is the short form of Conservative
a side is one party in a dispute or contest
a ration is a set amount allowed to each person

explanation.surface: The Tories pay out a fixed sum by way of benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' puts the allowance after the Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and business a consideration is the payment or reward given in return for something.

clue.text: Singer of inferior quality say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word, so we want a word that is pronounced the same but spelt differently

parts.note: base means low-grade or inferior, as in base metal

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a performer as second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a male vocalist with the lowest range, so the word names a kind of singer.

clue.text: Random tests for cannabis leading to arrest on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a vessel, so what precedes goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the crossword's usual vessel
pot is slang for cannabis
to check is to halt or arrest progress

explanation.surface: Police drug sweeps on a ship turn up cannabis and lead to someone being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, for steamship, is the crossword's usual ship; being on board one puts the other letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot checks are inspections made without warning on a sample chosen at random.

clue.text: What Boycott was to unfold before the Queen

parts.note: to unfold something is to open it out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a boycott and the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a Yorkshire and England cricketer who went in first to bat; boycott as a protest is the red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Boycott was a famous opening batsman, and the batter who starts an innings in cricket is called an opener.

clue.text: Careless errors by half-hearted criminal

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and half of it goes, so one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: slips are small mistakes
a hood is a gangster or thug

explanation.surface: A villain who is not fully committed keeps making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOD has the double O at its heart; losing half of that leaves HOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is sloppy and done without proper attention, so it is careless.

clue.text: Uncouth Roman peed in walkway

indicators.note: something uncouth is rough and unrefined, so the letters are knocked out of their proper order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boorish ancient Roman relieved himself in a public path.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a paved public path for strolling, often along a seafront, so it is a walkway.

clue.text: Poor Henry's taken in by a ruse at the same time

parts.note: mean can mean shabby or poor

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it, so one letter goes within another word

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An unfortunate man named Henry is fooled by a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person, but it is the unit of electrical inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means in the intervening time or simultaneously, so at the same time.

clue.text: Composer not wanting to embrace Russian leader

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece wraps its arms around the other

parts.note: off means not wanting, as in being off one's food

indicators.note: 'leader' keeps only the first letter of 'Russian'

parts.note: the leading letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A composer refuses to give a Russian head of state a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer of Carmina Burana.

clue.text: Go crazy in retirement

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: bats is informal for mad, as in bats in the belfry

explanation.surface: Someone loses their mind after giving up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in having a go.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to have a go, or an attempt, at it.

clue.text: Deal with the truth right away

parts.note: if something is so, it is true, as in that is so
RT is an abbreviation for right
out means away, as in out of the office

explanation.surface: A plea to face facts at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal with the truth' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Deal with'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to resolve or handle a problem or a person, which is dealing with them.

clue.text: Philosopher standing by Thucydides' initial study of routine drudgery

indicators.note: standing by means positioned next to, so the philosopher comes after the other pieces
initial means first, so only the opening letter of the historian's name is used

parts.note: the first letter of the Greek historian's name
to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher works beside the first chapter of an ancient history book.
explanation.walkthrough: Mill is the Victorian thinker John Stuart Mill; to read a subject is British usage for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is literally a wheel trodden endlessly, so figuratively it is monotonous work that goes nowhere.

clue.text: Performer finds time to appear in wicked satire

indicators.note: wicked suggests corruption, so the letters are perverted out of their proper order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An entertainer gets a moment in a cruel spoof.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer, so a performer.

clue.text: Organ recital's conclusion meets with exclamations of disgust and approval!

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of recital
ugh is a cry of revulsion
ole is a Spanish shout of approval

explanation.surface: An organ concert ends to mixed boos and cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ recital' suggests church music, but the organ is a body part. Lughole is British slang for ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lughole is a colloquial British word for the ear, which is an organ of the body.

clue.text: Accurately describe part of plane found in river

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
the fin is the vertical tail surface of an aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone describes a piece of aircraft wreckage recovered from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To define something is to state its nature or meaning precisely.

clue.text: Exhausted after b… brawl with bully

indicators.note: after means following, so the word for tired is placed behind the other pieces

parts.note: the lone letter shown before the dots
a row is a noisy quarrel or fight
beat means worn out, as in dead beat

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out after a scuffle with a thug, with an expletive politely blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots look like a censored swear word, but only the letter b is used. 'After' puts the tiredness last.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat someone is to intimidate them with stern words, which is to bully them.

clue.text: Finished without Rex however

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter has to be taken out of the word

parts.note: to be through is to be done with something
R is the abbreviation for Rex, the Latin for king

explanation.surface: Something is over, but the king is not involved after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Though, used at the end of a sentence, carries the same contrast as nevertheless or however.

clue.text: Attempt to remove top of box

indicators.note: removing the top of a down answer takes off its first letter

parts.note: a strongbox for keeping money or valuables

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lift the lid of a box.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer can mean an attempt or try, as in an offer at a shot, and to offer is to attempt.

clue.text: Concerned South American admits feeding ducks is not forbidden

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: to admit is to let something in, so the outer pieces take others inside
feeding something puts it inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, and nought looks like O
licit means lawful, the opposite of illicit
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A worried traveller from South America is told that feeding the ducks is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one idea but is two separate pieces that hold the rest between them; a duck in cricket is a score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitous means anxious or attentive about someone's welfare, so it is concerned.

clue.text: Animal's back seen in stream

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a wolf is a wild animal of the dog family

explanation.surface: The back of a creature is glimpsed in a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A flow is a steady moving current of liquid, like a stream.

clue.text: Happen to stop most of these coming from somewhere in Boeotia

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one word goes inside the other like a stopper
most of means nearly all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to be is to exist or take place, so happen

explanation.surface: An odd sentence about events halting and the source of something Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: THESE shortened to THES opens to take BE. Boeotia is a region of central Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was the chief city of ancient Boeotia in Greece, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: Law qualification essentially ludicrous for head of Geography

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a degree is an academic qualification

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the central letter is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of ludicrous

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter of the subject is meant

parts.note: the first letter of Geography

explanation.surface: A law degree is ridiculous compared with being head of the geography department.
explanation.walkthrough: The C from the centre of ludicrous takes the place of the G in DEGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order with the force of law, so it can stand for a law.
